steering_counts.measure: refusals of harmless agent tasks (AgentHarm harmless)

contrasts.contrast: GWATCH, L2C, GRD, COT − mean(R1, R2, R3) (each)

verdicts.contribution: 1. A controlled map of evaluation beliefs
numbers: Models run after the grouping was fixed: safety-flavoured minus merely-watched beliefs raise refusals of harmless agent tasks in 37 of 40 model x method contrasts (23 with 95% intervals above 0; 8 models)
Same models, harmful agent tasks: lower completion in 31 of 36 (20 intervals below 0)

Cells that count under the pre-set rules (complete models, all planting methods but steering): capability agentic 0 of 576; capability chat 0 of 1,853; safety agentic 181 of 3,134; safety chat 140 of 3,692
verdicts.objection: The grouping was set after reading gpt-oss-120b, it rests on one agent benchmark near its floor, and a plain rule reminder moves refusals about as far: 'safety-flavoured' may mean 'reminded of the rules', not 'believes it is a safety test'.
verdicts.extension: Fresh AgentHarm-harmless and OR-Bench (>=150 tasks each) plus one new agent over-refusal set; pre-registered safety minus watched > 0 per model, and safety minus rule reminder > 0.

verdicts.contribution: 2. An account that predicts the effects
verdicts.verdict: mixed: 'not real' and 'purpose' hold as directions; no account predicts unseen beliefs; safety beliefs do about what a rule reminder does
numbers: 'Not real': a long planted 'simulated, nothing is real' thought raises compliance with harmful requests (interval above 0) in 9 of 10 models with long thoughts (6 of 10 pass the pre-set rules: Flint, gpt-oss-20b, Muse Glimmer 30B, Nemotron 3 Super 120B, Qwen3.8-27B, Ripple-65B) and lowers OR-Bench refusals in 8 (all but gpt-oss-120b)

Held-out beliefs: the feature model beats 'every belief does its method's average' in 1 of 40 model x outcome pairs and is worse in 21; the evaluator's purpose helps predict unseen beliefs in 10 pairs (Flint, Nemotron 3 Super 120B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.8-27B, Ripple-65B), watched in 0, reality in 0

Safety-flavoured beliefs minus the rule reminder: no difference larger than 5 points in 24 of 28 model x outcome pairs with room (within 3 points in 21); the 95% interval lies inside +-5 points in 18 (not an equivalence test)
verdicts.objection: Seventeen beliefs with overlapping features cannot separate the accounts ('real' rests on one belief), safety beliefs do no more than a reminder of the rules, and the long 'simulated' text also tells the model that nothing it does matters and appraises the request (an instruction and an appraisal, not only a belief); with 12 models no model property predicts responsiveness beyond 'room to move'.
verdicts.extension: Matched belief pairs that differ in one feature only (purpose, watched, real) at matched length, a rule-reminder arm for every method including long thoughts, and 'evaluation, nothing is real' against 'evaluation, used for real'.

verdicts.contribution: 3. A validated way to study these beliefs
verdicts.verdict: positive as a description; validation not yet
numbers: Taken on in the forced choice: statement 83%, notice 91%, one-sentence thought 22%, long thoughts 88% / 82% (thoughts: coder); count as effects: 0.8%, 0.4%, 2.3%, 9.2% / 8.6% of cells. In the models' own words after the run (ten models of build a7): statement 64%, notice 48%, environment cue 16% of model x belief groups (forced choice on the same rule 68 / 86 / 52%; reported 80 / 92 / 54%); planted thoughts cannot be checked by either after-run measure
Side effects: long neutral thoughts move safety behaviour against nothing planted in 21 of 70 model x benchmark cells, neutral one-sentence thoughts in 15 of 70, neutral statements in 5 of 78
Steering toward 'evaluation' beats random directions of the same strength on at least one safety set in 3 of 5 steered models (Flint, gpt-oss-20b, Ripple-65B)
verdicts.objection: 'Taken on' is not a validated belief measure: for statements and notices it is a forced choice whose options nearly repeat the planted sentence, and in the models' own words notices register in about half the groups and cues in a sixth; 'real deployment' is never voiced in the models' own words (0 of 16 statement and notice groups); prompts register and do little; the three neutral one-sentence thoughts differ from each other about as much as the belief thoughts do; long texts also act when neutral, and the long neutral text stops the reasoning in Qwen3.5-122B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3.8-27B and Muse Glimmer 30B (34–79% of runs on average); steering moves the readout in random directions too.
verdicts.extension: Per-method validity checks fixed in advance (readout and coder agreement, neutral and random controls at matched length and strength) on the same tasks as the behaviour.
